PG.rationale: PG is a high-quality defensive franchise with durable brands, disciplined capital allocation (70-year dividend streak, ~$15B annual shareholder returns), and solid balance sheet (equity grew to $54.73B). However, the current earnings trajectory is decelerating: Q3 FY26 showed sequential revenue -4.4%, EPS -8.4%, and margin compression across gross (51.3%→49.5%), operating (24.2%→21.6%), and net (19.5%→18.6%) tiers. The YoY growth (+7.4% revenue, +5.8% EPS) is partly inflated by a one-time Glad JV gain; underlying core EPS growth was only ~3%. Significant cost headwinds—$400M tariff costs in FY26 and a projected $1B oil headwind in FY27—are suppressing earnings and led management to guide toward the lower end of the $6.83–$7.09 core EPS range. Valuation at PE 23.8x is near the bottom of its 12-month range (21.7–26.3x), offering modest reversion potential, but the earnings yield of 4.2% sits below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.49%, limiting multiple expansion. The 7,000-job restructuring and leadership transition add execution uncertainty. A near-term catalyst exists in the Q4 FY26 earnings call on July 29, 2026, but consensus expects Q4 EPS of ~$1.43 (down ~3.4% YoY), which is unlikely to spark a positive re-rating. Oil price decline to ~$70/bbl could ease input costs, but the $1B FY27 headwind guidance already reflects this environment. Net: a stable, high-quality franchise in a temporary earnings trough, modestly cheap vs its own history but not compellingly so given the deceleration and cost headwinds.
